screening_results.reason: Although this is an fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults and reports group-level voxelwise task contrasts (AV, VIS, AUD vs rest, and AV vs ApV), the fMRI acquisition used a split-sagittal, partial-volume protocol that explicitly excluded medial regions and other large portions of the brain (e.g., medial frontal/parietal cortex, fusiform and early visual cortex). The review’s inclusion criterion requires at least one group-level, univariate whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map generalizable to healthy adults. Because the imaging did not provide whole-brain coverage, the reported voxelwise results are limited to a restricted volume and do not meet the ‘whole-brain’ requirement. All other criteria (healthy adult sample, group-level voxelwise analyses) are met, but failure to provide whole-brain coverage necessitates exclusion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (prosody perception/production and empathy) in healthy adults (n=19; age 18–58). Group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts are reported (e.g., “happy–neutral”, “question–neutral”) using random-effects analyses with FDR correction and cluster reporting; results and coordinates are described in the text and supplementary materials. The paper does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity analyses, and reports healthy-group task activation maps generalizable to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (20 scanned; mean age 25.7, within 17–65). The task probes social-related processing (guilt memory vs hypothetical social scenarios; involves social cognition, agency, and perception/understanding of others). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (e.g., guilt memories vs neutral memories; guilt memories vs guilt hypotheticals) thresholded at p<0.001 with cluster extent and reports peak coordinates and figures; SPM8 second-level analyses were performed and whole-brain activations (posterior cingulate, inferior frontal cortices, etc.) are described. Results for the healthy/control group are reported separately and are generalizable to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not clinical-only, not non-empirical). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a social task (Ultimatum Game) probing social decision-making (cooperation/fairness). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (N≈51; mean ages ~31, within 17–65) with results reported separately for healthy groups. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (pre/post training GLMs, conjunctions, interaction contrasts) with voxelwise statistical maps and coordinates (FDR-corrected results, Tables S1/S2 and figures). Although ROI and PPI analyses are also present, they supplement—not replace—whole-brain task activation results. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, participants are within age range and healthy). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study uses fMRI in healthy adult participants and includes social tasks (theory-of-mind and social attribution), but it does not report a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy group. Analyses rely on localized ICA applied within a temporoparietal ROI and regression of IC time courses, with subsequent seed-to-voxel functional connectivity maps. These are ROI-decomposed and connectivity results rather than the required whole-brain voxelwise task activation contrasts (e.g., GLM group maps or within-group voxelwise contrasts). Because the paper lacks an unmasked, whole-brain healthy-group task activation map, it fails the ‘whole-brain evidence’ inclusion criterion and must be excluded.

Although the study is an fMRI investigation of a social processing task (face encoding/recognition) in healthy adults, it reports only ROI-based analyses focused on the amygdala. The Methods explicitly state the analysis focused on an a priori amygdala ROI and extraction of parameter estimates; no group-level, univariate whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical maps or whole-brain coordinate tables for the healthy group are reported. This violates the inclusion requirement for at least one whole-brain healthy-group task activation map. (Note: the sample includes both young adults and older adults >65, but the primary exclusion is ROI-only reporting.)

This is an fMRI study of social processing (Social Feedback task) in a healthy sample (final N=56; age range 17–20, mean 18) which falls within the review’s eligible age range (17–65). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., positive>neutral, negative>neutral; whole-brain FWE-corrected p<0.05) using SPM8 and random-effects analyses. Results are not limited to ROIs or connectivity-only analyses, and healthy-group activation maps/contrasts are clearly reported and generalizable to the healthy sample. No exclusion criteria are violated (not clinical-only, not resting-state/ROI-only, and includes whole-brain task activations). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

The study reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (20 participants analyzed, ages 18–55). The task is a social-related imitate/observe emotional faces paradigm targeting perception/understanding of others and empathy. The paper describes whole-brain voxelwise analyses: a univariate GLM in SPM8 (reported as showing similar whole-brain patterns) and spatio-temporal PLS maps with voxelwise bootstrap-ratio maps rendered on MNI brain. Results present group-level spatial activation patterns and brain–behavior correlations across the whole brain. The sample falls within the 17–65 age range, and results for the healthy group are reported. The study is empirical fMRI work and does not rely solely on ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=30 females, age 19–39) investigating social-related processing (kinship, moral dilemma, mentalizing). It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise results: inter-subject correlation (ISC) maps across the whole brain and a GLM-based whole-brain analysis of a moral-dilemma decision task, with multiple-comparison correction and cluster tables; unthresholded maps are available on NeuroVault. The sample is within the 17–65 range and results are reported for the healthy group. The study is not ROI-only, not resting-state-only, and presents generalizable healthy-group task activations, meeting all inclusion criteria.

Although the study is an fMRI investigation of social evaluation in healthy adult participants (N=36, mean age 22) and reports within-group task contrasts, all reported neuroimaging results are small-volume/ROI-corrected within a vACC mask. The paper does not present or describe unmasked, whole-brain group-level voxelwise task activation maps or whole-brain coordinate tables for healthy adults. Therefore it fails the inclusion requirement that at least one group-level whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map be reported; it appears to report only ROI-restricted findings.

Although the study uses fMRI on healthy adult participants and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (within-group male vs female stimuli with FWE-corrected clusters), the experimental paradigm investigates sexual arousal and reward-related responses to erotic stimuli to study sexual orientation. The primary constructs are sexual incentive motivation and reward (ventral striatum) rather than social-related processing (e.g., affiliation/attachment, social communication, or perception/understanding of others as social agents). Thus it does not meet the meta-analysis’ requirement for a social-related task. Therefore the study should be excluded.

The study uses task-based fMRI (naturalistic movie viewing of Toy Story) that probes social-cognitive processing. A healthy adult group (final N=21 adults) within the 17–65 range is reported separately. The paper presents whole-brain, group-level maps (within-group inter-subject correlation maps and Adult vs Child contrasts) with peak coordinates and multiple-threshold cluster correction; results are described for the adult (healthy) group and are generalizable (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Although the analytic approach uses inter-subject correlation rather than a traditional GLM, it yields univariate, voxel/nodewise whole-brain statistical maps for the healthy adult group, satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy-only samples, or non-empirical paper) apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult samples (Experiment 1: N=50, ages 19–34; Experiment 2: N=23, ages 18–30). Tasks probe social interaction perception (interactive vs. non-interactive, cooperation vs. competition) using task-evoked stimuli. The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., social interaction > independent actions) with surface-based random-effects group analysis and FDR-corrected results in the pSTS; coordinates/thresholding and group maps are described. Analyses include whole-brain and ROI-based results, meeting the requirement for a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map. No exclusion criteria are violated.

This study reports task-based fMRI of a social process (empathic accuracy/EAT) in healthy adults (final sample n=34, ages ~20–30). It provides group-level, whole-brain, univariate voxelwise analyses (random-effects models; TFCE FWE-corrected results reported) including contrasts (emotional > neutral, happy vs sad), parametric modulation by empathic accuracy, and time-series correlations with continuous intensity ratings. Results are presented as significant whole-brain clusters (tables/figures) generalizable to a healthy adult group. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, healthy adult group reported separately). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This paper reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=59 across three studies) investigating socially relevant processing (person knowledge, socially relevant concept words). Group-level, univariate whole-brain contrasts are reported (e.g., social > non-social semantics) with voxelwise thresholds, cluster correction, peak coordinates, and whole-brain figures described in the text. Results for the healthy control participants are presented separately and generalizable to healthy adults. The study is empirical, not ROI-only, and does not violate exclusion criteria (no resting-state/seed-only analyses, not limited to special populations). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (1) fMRI during a social-related task (approach–avoidance task with social vs nonsocial positive/negative scenes); (2) sample consists of healthy adult participants (male, ages ~21, N analyzed per group reported), with no clinical subgroup required; (3) authors created and analyzed task-evoked first-level contrasts and conducted second-level group analyses and report exploratory whole-brain results beyond a priori ROIs (text states whole-brain analyses reported at P<.05 corrected), providing univariate, group-level task-evoked statistical maps generalizable to healthy adults. Although many focal findings used ROI/SVC, whole-brain analyses are explicitly reported, and the study is not limited to connectivity or ROI-only reporting. Therefore it is eligible for inclusion.

While the study uses task-based fMRI of social impression formation in healthy adult participants (N=60, mean age 23.8) and meets sample and task criteria, the paper does not report any group-level, univariate whole-brain (voxelwise) task-evoked statistical map or coordinate table for the healthy group. The reported neuroimaging results are multivariate PLS analyses and bootstrapped brain–behavior correlations; univariate GLM methods are described and univariate results are referenced as coming from a prior analysis, but no univariate whole-brain activation map/contrast (or coordinates/tables/figures) from this study’s healthy group is presented in the manuscript itself. Therefore it fails the requirement for reporting a within-group univariate whole-brain task effect.

This is an empirical fMRI study of joint action (leader/follower) tapping social cognition (perception/understanding of others, mentalizing networks such as TPJ, PCC, mPFC are explicitly investigated). Sample: 18 healthy adult participants (mean age ~40), within 17–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., Leading>Following, Following>Leading, conjunction [Leading>Rest]∩[Following>Rest]) with statistical thresholds, cluster corrections and Talairach coordinates presented in figures/tables. It is not ROI-only, nor resting-state/connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain maps are clearly reported. Although authors note exploratory/limited power, all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria are violated.

Although the study uses task fMRI of social processing (trustworthiness appraisal) and includes a healthy adult control group (n=17), the paper does not clearly report an unmasked, group-level whole-brain task activation map that is explicitly identified as coming from the healthy/control group. The manuscript mainly reports (1) whole-brain analyses across all participants, (2) between-group contrasts (BPD vs controls), and (3) ROI and mask-based analyses for the amygdala and subject-specific masks. Because the inclusion criterion requires at least one clearly reported whole-brain, univariate healthy-group task effect generalizable to healthy adults (not only ROI or between-group contrasts), this study does not meet all inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI hyperscanning study of real-time mutual eye contact, a clear social communication task (shared attention/perception of others). The sample comprises healthy adults (n=30 analyzed for fMRI; mean age ~21.7), within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate GLM results (LIVE > REPLAY contrast) with cluster-level FWE correction and detailed coordinates/figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Although additional connectivity and interbrain analyses are included, they do not replace the presence of univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps. No exclusion criteria are violated. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related Face Processing Task (fearful vs. neutral faces) in healthy adults (n=49; ages 18–33). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (Fearful>Neutral and Neutral>Fearful) and associated statistical maps/results using TFCE with FWE correction, and provides coordinates and whole-brain analyses (including exploratory whole-brain and median-split comparisons). Results are clearly reported for the healthy control/participant group and are generalizable to healthy adults. The study is not ROI-only and includes univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps, so it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (social exclusion/ostracism via Cyberball) in a sample of healthy adult participants (female, mean age 21.7). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise univariate whole-brain analyses and provides peak coordinates for significant effects (e.g., right AI, rTPJ, subACC) derived from contrasts involving the healthy participant groups; whole-brain analyses were conducted (initial threshold p<0.001 uncorrected) with clusters reported (SVC FWE-corrected) and coordinates supplied. The task and contrasts are clearly social-related and the results are generalizable to healthy adults. Although many reported effects are between healthy-subgroup contrasts (support-type vs no support), these are univariate, group-level, voxelwise maps in healthy adults and reported with coordinates, satisfying the inclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction perception in healthy adults (n=21, ages 18–35) using task-evoked functional MRI. The paradigm directly investigates social interaction processing (arguing, celebrating, laughing) and reports group-level analyses: whole-brain GLMs were run (used to generate beta maps and to create group-constrained, whole-brain localizer contrasts such as interaction>scrambled, bodies>objects, faces>objects, mentalizing>pain) and these localizer contrasts are described and visualized (supplementary materials) to define ROIs. Although the primary reported effects are multivariate (ROI-based MVPA and whole-brain searchlight), the paper clearly includes group-level, univariate, whole-brain task contrasts from healthy participants (the localizers) that meet the review’s requirement for a group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked map. The sample falls within the eligible age range and no exclusion criteria (connectivity-only, patient-only, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

Meets all inclusion criteria: This is an empirical task-based fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=31 for fMRI; ages 18–35). The task probes social-related processing (perception/understanding of others) by presenting faces with/without disfigurement during a gender-judgement cover task. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate voxelwise contrasts (non-parametric SnPM analysis) with cluster-level FWE correction (p<0.05) showing increased/decreased activations; results are described and shown in figures/tables. It is not ROI-only, not resting-state or connectivity-only, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are generalizable to healthy adults, so INCLUDED.

The study used fMRI during a social (trust-game) task, but the sample consists of male adolescents aged 13–19 with no separately reported healthy adult (17–65) subgroup. The review requires at least one healthy adult group (age 17–65) reported separately. Although the paper includes whole-brain task analyses, these are not clearly reported as univariate whole-brain maps for a healthy adult control group generalizable to adults. Therefore it fails the sample-age inclusion criterion (and thus the required healthy adult whole-brain reporting).

This study uses task-based fMRI during a social/neuroeconomic paradigm (prisoner’s dilemma) probing social behavior and social cognition. It includes a healthy adult control group (n=15, ages 18–50) reported separately. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation maps and results for controls (e.g., significant activations in right fusiform gyrus, right superior frontal gyrus, left insula, left superior temporal gyrus during decision-making), as well as one-sample and per-group t-tests and full-factorial analyses (FWE-corrected whole-brain thresholds). Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. Age range, task relevance, and whole-brain healthy-group contrasts satisfy the inclusion criteria. Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

Although the study includes a healthy typically-developing (TD) adult control group (age range within 17–65) and uses task-based fMRI during a social (dynamic facial expression) paradigm, it does not report an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map or within-group contrast specifically for the healthy/control group. The paper reports ROI-based group analyses and whole-brain analyses only as between-group (ASD vs TD) comparisons (which yielded no significant group-difference clusters) and focuses on effective connectivity (DCM). Because the inclusion criteria require at least one healthy-group whole-brain univariate task-evoked map (reportable as coordinates/figures/tables), and this is not provided, the study must be excluded.

This is an fMRI study of action perception (perception/understanding of others’ hand actions), a social-related construct. It includes multiple groups of healthy adult participants (total n=79 across Experiments 1–3 and 31 controls in Experiment 5) with group-level, voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., ActionOBS–CtrlOBS and weight discrimination contrasts) reported whole-brain (with maps, conjunctions, and thresholding described). Although a patient group (SCA6) is included, results for healthy controls are reported separately. The paper provides univariate, generalizable healthy-group activation maps (figures, thresholds, ROIs), meeting the review’s inclusion criteria. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, or lack of healthy whole-brain task maps) are violated.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=9, mean age 24) that examines perception of others’ eye gaze—a social communication cue—using task-based fMRI. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation contrasts (face vs control; gaze vs identity; averted vs direct gaze) with cluster thresholds and coordinates, and presents regional activations and statistical comparisons generalizable to healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the full text is complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study uses fMRI in a social face perception task (satisfies I3). However, the available content does not provide participant ages or confirm that participants were healthy adults in the 17–65 range (I4 not verifiable), nor does it report or provide evidence of a group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation map for the healthy group (I5 not verifiable). The abstract emphasizes ROI-based analysis of the amygdala, raising the possibility that only ROI results are reported, but the full methods/results needed to confirm whole-brain results are missing. Because one or more mandatory inclusion criteria cannot be verified from the provided full text, the study is excluded pending access to the complete article.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Based on available abstract: I3 is satisfied (task-based fMRI of social judgments: empathy and forgivability). I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65) cannot be confirmed — the abstract states 'ten volunteers' but gives no ages or explicit statement that they are healthy adults within 17–65. I5 (reporting of group-level, univariate whole-brain voxelwise healthy-group task maps) cannot be verified from the truncated text: although the abstract lists activated regions, the complete methods/results are not available to confirm these are whole-brain, group-level, univariate maps (rather than ROI or other analyses). Because not all inclusion criteria can be confirmed and the full text is incomplete, the study is excluded pending full-text availability. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are explicitly met from the available information.

The study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (final N=14, ages 18–30) while they made social evaluations (trustworthiness judgments) of faces, directly addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of others). The paper presents group-level, random-effects, voxelwise SPM analyses with reported statistical maps/coordinates (parametric contrasts, whole-brain thresholds, small-volume corrections) that are generalizable to the healthy adult group. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This study reports task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=12, ages 20–51) performing a social attribution task (self- vs other-responsibility; self-serving bias), directly addressing social-related processing (perception/understanding of self/others). The paper presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain univariate contrasts (internal vs external attributions; self-serving vs non-self-serving) with tables, figures, and coordinates; results are explicitly from the healthy/control group. Although sample size is small and many analyses used fixed-effects models (authors acknowledge limitations), whole-brain voxelwise activation maps (P<0.05 corrected) are reported and described in the text and tables. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets the review inclusion criteria and is eligible for inclusion.

This paper reports an event-related fMRI experiment probing social processing (moral status of faces learned via iterative Prisoner's Dilemma) during an explicit task (gender judgments) — meeting the social-related task requirement. The sample includes healthy adult participants (scanned cohort n=11, ages 21–36) with behavioral and imaging results reported for the healthy group separately. The authors report group-level, random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts and provide tables of coordinates and statistical maps referenced in the text (univariate task-evoked activation maps in ROIs and whole-brain descriptive results). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI task in which healthy adult participants (N=13, mean age 27.2) passively viewed realistic social interaction video clips (social relational vs alone segments and rest). Group-level, whole-brain voxelwise statistical contrasts are reported (relational vs. alone; relational vs. rest) with correction for multiple spatial comparisons and clusters/peaks given in figures and Table 1. The methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text provided. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based fMRI of social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain univariate healthy-group results. No exclusion criteria are met.

This empirical fMRI study examined social processing (mutual vs. averted gaze) in healthy adult participants using a task that clearly probes social perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation maps (t-statistic activation maps displayed on a standard brain; voxel-based analyses described in Methods and Results), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain univariate results. The sample comprises healthy young adults (fMRI group described and reported separately), and whole-brain results are presented in figures and text. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Note: sample size is small and several subjects were excluded for motion, but this does not violate inclusion criteria. Therefore the study meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (cooperation vs competition) in healthy adults (N=12, ages 21–28) using a task that manipulates social interaction (meets I3 and I4). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain univariate analyses and direct task contrasts (cooperation vs independent, competition vs independent, cooperation vs competition) with voxelwise thresholds and tables/figures of activations (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met: whole-brain results are reported (not ROI-only), not only connectivity/resting-state, and healthy adult group results are clearly presented. The provided full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete (fulltext_incomplete=false). Therefore the study qualifies for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

The paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (evaluative judgments of self-conscious moral emotions: guilt and embarrassment) in healthy adults. Sample: 19 healthy right-handed adult participants (mean ages within 17–65). The analyses include group-level, random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (Guilt − Neutral, Embarrassment − Neutral, and direct contrasts) with coordinates and figures reported. Results are presented as univariate whole-brain statistical maps and tables of peak coordinates, making them generalizable to healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and does not meet any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, or non-empirical study). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). The study likely used fMRI for social cognition (theory of mind), so I3 is met. However I cannot confirm participant characteristics/age range or that healthy adult group results are reported separately (I4), nor can I confirm that a group-level, univariate whole-brain voxelwise task activation map is reported for the healthy group (I5/I6). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are demonstrably met based on available information. Because core methodological details and results are not available in the provided full text, I must exclude per screening rules until full text is obtained.

This is an event-related fMRI study of self-face recognition (a social-cognitive task addressing Perception and Understanding of Self). It tested a healthy adult sample (N=10; mean age 26.9) and reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise univariate contrasts (self>other, other>self) with cluster-corrected thresholding and tables of MNI coordinates. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it satisfies all required inclusion criteria and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social cognition (impression formation of people vs objects) in healthy adults (N=14; mean age 20.6), meeting the review objective. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate voxelwise contrasts (e.g., person-impression > other trials; impressions > sequencing) analyzed with SPM99, voxelwise thresholds and MNI coordinates/tables are provided. Therefore it satisfies I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample within 17–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level univariate task activation maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and contrasts clearly described). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an event-related BOLD fMRI study of self-face recognition (Perception and Understanding of Self), a social-related construct, in healthy adults. The sample comprises 12 healthy right-handed adult males (mean age ~19), with results reported for the healthy group. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain voxelwise contrasts (e.g., self vs. familiar, familiar vs. unknown, distracter vs. null) with SPM maps and tables/figures of coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within 17–65, empirical fMRI data present).

This is an fMRI experiment in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 24.4) examining processing of angry prosody (social communication/perception of others), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain SPM2 random-effects analyses with contrasts and coordinates (whole-brain results presented in text, figures, and Table 1), satisfying whole-brain evidence reporting. Healthy adult group results are reported separately and generalizable (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so the article is complete for screening. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied; no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (Theory of Mind and empathy) using a visual cartoon task in healthy adult volunteers (N=13; age range 19–36). The paper reports group-level, random-effects, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2) with thresholding and tables/figures of activation foci for contrasts (ToM−Physical1, Empathy−Physical2), conjunctions, and interactions—meeting whole-brain reporting requirements. Participants are healthy adults within the 17–65 range. No exclusion criteria are met: results are not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not limited to between-group contrasts, and this is original empirical fMRI data. Full text material (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is a task-based fMRI study investigating social-related processing (gaze and social facial expressions) using virtual characters, with healthy adult participants (n=18, mean age 25.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses (contrasts, statistical maps, tables of coordinates, and figures) and provides results generalizable to healthy adults. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate maps), and I6 (reporting coordinates/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-only, not between-group-only, participants are within age range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This fMRI study investigates perception/understanding of self (detection of visual feedback ownership), matching the review construct (I3). Participants are healthy adults (16 recruited; 15 analyzed) aged 20–28, satisfying sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, univariate, whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (e.g., Aa–As, Pa–Ps, ±((Aa–As)-(Pa–Ps))) with cluster- and voxel-level thresholds and tables/figures of activated clusters, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements (I5, I6). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text is complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (spontaneous retrieval of affective person knowledge during face perception) in healthy adult participants (ages 18–32). The paper reports voxel-wise, group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses with reported coordinates and cluster statistics for contrasts of theoretical interest (faces associated with behaviors vs novel faces; negative vs positive; disgusting vs aggressive). The methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate task-evoked maps reported), and I6 (coordinates and maps described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The provided content is limited to an abstract/summary and metadata; core article content (methods, participant details, and full results/whole-brain maps) is not present. Based on available information: (a) Inclusion met: I3 (study uses fMRI in a social-related task — processing facial expressions/identity). (b) Inclusion not confirmed: I4 (sample ages/healthy adult group not explicitly reported in the supplied text), I5 (no explicit reporting of a group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked statistical map in the provided content). No exclusion criteria are explicitly met from the available text. Because the full text is incomplete, key inclusion criteria cannot be verified and the study must be excluded from the review at this stage pending full-text access.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction (reactive aggression) in healthy adults using a competitive reaction-time paradigm (social-related task). Sample: healthy adult males (initial N=16, final N=14 after exclusions), mean age 28.6, within 17–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM2; random-effects t-statistics; voxelwise thresholds, coordinates, tables and figures) for multiple task conditions (retaliation, watching opponent, receiving stimuli). Whole-brain statistical maps and coordinate tables are reported and described for the healthy group. Group-level, whole-brain random-effects SPM analyses are reported, with voxel-level FWE-corrected results and coordinates (tables and figures) for affiliative versus nonaffiliative and valence contrasts. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social/attachment processing: mothers listened to infant cry (a social/attachment-related task) during functional MRI and results relate to attachment behaviors. Participants are healthy adults (primiparous mothers, mean age 24.1; screened with SCID and no participants met criteria for current major depressive episode at time of scanning), satisfying the healthy adult group requirement. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise group-level analyses (FSL/FLAME), with thresholding and cluster coordinates presented (Table 1, figures), and describes task-evoked maps for the healthy group. Full article contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports an fMRI study of empathy/perspective-taking (social cognition) using healthy adult participants (n=18, ages 21–31). The methods describe whole-brain, group-level voxelwise analyses (first- and second-level SPM analyses), with cluster- and peak-level FWE-corrected results and coordinates reported in tables/figures (e.g., Self vs Other, View-Pain vs View-No-Pain contrasts, conjunction analyses). The study therefore satisfies the review scope and reports whole-brain healthy-group task activation maps in standard coordinate tables and figures. The provided full text includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary figures, so the full text appears complete.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study that includes social reasoning tasks (theory of mind / emotion understanding) presented as texts and videos. Sample: 45 healthy adult participants (mean age 20.5, range 19–23), satisfying the healthy adult age criterion. Whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses are reported (GLM, random-effects analyses, multiple comparison correction) with peak coordinates provided (Appendix A) and figures showing task > rest and domain contrasts; results are generalizable to the healthy population. The paper is not ROI-only, not resting-only, and reports univariate group-level whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, appendices) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (perception of emotional facial expressions) with healthy adult human participants (N=23, ages 24–34). The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses in humans with cluster-wise correction and presents whole-brain significance maps and stereotactic coordinates. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate results), and I6 (acceptable reporting via maps/coordinates). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (action observation, mirror-neuron and mentalizing systems) in a sample of healthy adults (N=19, ages 18–32), satisfying the sample criterion. Analyses are group-level random-effects voxelwise contrasts and the manuscript explicitly states that whole-brain results and details about the mask are provided in the Supplemental Material; reporting of group-level statistical maps (cluster results/coordinates) is provided in the text/tables, satisfying the whole-brain evidence criterion (I5) and allowing supplemental reporting (I6). The task is clearly social-related (mentalizing/understanding others), satisfying I3. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only restriction, no connectivity/rest-only focus, no between-group-only contrasts, participants are within 17–65 range, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an fMRI study of social cognitive processing (visual perspective taking) in healthy adult participants (mean age 22.4; n=16 after exclusions). The paper reports task-evoked, group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., Inconsistent Other > Consistent Other; Consistent Self > Consistent Other) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and tables/figures of results. Healthy-group results are reported and generalizable to healthy adults. Full article content (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical task-based fMRI study examining action observation and execution (mirror responses), which maps onto social cognitive processes (Perception and Understanding of Others). The sample comprises 21 healthy adult participants (mean age 24), within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, random-effects, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (mentions a whole-brain analysis at p<0.001 uncorrected and reports peak coordinates and clusters), in addition to ROI results. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and thus appears complete. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social cognition (contrast of interactive vs. observational social stimuli) using task-based BOLD in healthy adult participants (N=22; mean age 25). The methods describe group-level random-effects whole-brain analyses (Three-Way repeated-measures whole-brain ANOVA) and report task-evoked effects; exploratory whole-brain results (e.g., early visual V1) are described in the text. ROI analyses/SVC were applied for hypothesis-driven tests, but whole-brain group-level testing was performed and reported. The sample falls within the 17–65 range and results are reported for the healthy group. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) are met. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and is suitable for inclusion in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study that directly manipulates social information (trustworthiness judgments) during a task and reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate voxelwise analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA) with cluster correction and tables of peak coordinates. Sample consists of healthy adults (N analyzed=14, mean age 22) within the 17–65 range. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria are satisfied and no exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition (empathy/perception of others’ pain), conducted in healthy adult participants (n≈36, ages ~21). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (painful vs non-painful stimuli) with FDR-corrected maps and tables of activations, and describes these results in the text (whole-brain analyses in pre- and post-priming sessions). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an event-related fMRI study of face gender perception, a form of social perception (Perception and Understanding of Others) using healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 19–42). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise random-effects analyses (contrast gender-different > gender-same) with reported clusters/coordinates and figures (right CoS, left precuneus, right lateral occipital gyrus, etc.). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level univariate voxelwise results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (interpersonal resource conflict) in healthy adults (final N=17, mean age 23.5) that reports group-level whole-brain univariate activation contrasts (e.g., Conflict > No Conflict, interaction Human×Conflict) with thresholding and tables/figures. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates neural correlates of abstract vs. concrete mindsets using tasks that engage social cognition (Why-How task probes ‘why’ people perform actions, recruiting the mentalizing network). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (uses fMRI during social-related tasks involving perception/understanding of others), I4 (healthy adult sample: 24 right-handed participants, ages 18–27), I5 (reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses with one-sample t-tests and voxelwise thresholds; conjunction analyses reported), I6 (whole-brain results reported in text, tables, and figures). No exclusion criteria apply: analyses are whole-brain (not ROI-only), not limited to connectivity-only or between-group-only contrasts, participants are within age range, and the paper contains original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Appendices).

This full-text reports an fMRI study of social perception (comparisons of physical attractiveness of other people), meeting the review objective. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task is social-related: beauty comparisons of other persons), I4 (sample: 25 healthy adult participants, mean age 23.46 within 17–65), I5 (group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts reported; voxelwise and cluster-level thresholds given), I6 (whole-brain results reported with coordinates/tables and described in text). Full text includes Introduction, Methods (fMRI acquisition and preprocessing), Results (whole-brain and ROI analyses with coordinates), and Discussion; fulltext appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore include for the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study using a social interaction task (modified cyberball) with healthy adult participants (N=15, ages ~24), meeting I3 and I4. The paper reports group-level whole-brain analyses: univariate SPM group analyses (reported as null for the interaction) and an exploratory whole-brain searchlight (voxelwise random-effects group analysis) with corrected significant clusters (coordinates and t-values reported), satisfying the requirement for whole-brain, voxelwise reporting (I5) and acceptable reporting formats (I6). The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about groups and individuals) in healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: n=25, ages 19–27; Experiment 2: n=14, ages 18–23), satisfying sample criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., group mental > group physical; member mental > member physical) with voxel-wise thresholds, ROI extent thresholds, and tables/figures of results, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (scanned group N=38, ages 19–31) using a social task (real-world speed-dating) that probes affiliation/attachment and perception of others. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts and statistical maps (main effects and contrasts such as Yes > No, Match > Unrequited, violations of expectation) with tables of coordinates and thresholding details. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state only, not a between-group-only comparison, age range within 17–65, not a non-empirical paper). Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6.

This fMRI study investigates social communication (communicative vs private intentions) using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (N=23, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., CInt > PInt, interaction effects) with stereotaxic coordinates, thresholds, and tables/figures, and additionally reports PPI connectivity. Thus it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate results), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly reported). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group only, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (handholding/social regulation of threat) in a healthy adult sample (N=22; mean age 23.6). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (cluster-wise tests using FSL/FLAME with Z>2.3, p<.05), and presents ROI/coordinate results in Table 1 and figures. All inclusion criteria are satisfied (I3: fMRI social task; I4: healthy adult sample 17–65; I5: group-level whole-brain univariate task-evoked results reported; I6: whole-brain results reported in table/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion provided).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (laughter perception) in healthy adults (n=18, mean age 26), meeting the population criterion. The task explicitly probes social-related processing (laughter type categorization versus bout counting), satisfying the social-related task requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., CSL>TIC, TIC>CSL, CAT>COU) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction and provides coordinates/tables/figures, meeting whole-brain evidence and acceptable reporting formats. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within 17–65, empirical data present). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication (imitation of communicative gestures), meeting the review objective. The sample comprises healthy adults (20 analyzed; mean age 24.6), satisfying the age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (e.g., IMI>CT, S>NS) with voxel coordinates and cluster-level correction (Monte Carlo), and presents results across whole-brain contrasts in tables and figures. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study should be included.

This empirical fMRI study examines neural responses to others’ suffering (social cognition/empathy) in healthy adult participants (aged 18–45) and reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task analyses (e.g., Group × Redistribution Rank interaction; whole-brain corrected results identifying IPC and DLPFC), along with ROI/PPI follow-ups. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (reporting group-level whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked maps/results), and I6 (results clearly described in text/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing in healthy adults (N=31, ages 18–26) using a gambling task where participants played for self, best friend, and an antagonist. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (within-subject ANOVAs) with voxelwise results, tables of coordinates, figures, and whole-brain Person × Outcome interaction and main effects (with small-volume correction reported where applicable). All core article sections (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (interns N=19, mean age 20.55; producers N=79, mean age 20.54) examining social communication/mentalizing processes during a task in which participants considered recommending ideas (social-related task). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects univariate analyses and reports voxelwise results and coordinates (thresholded whole-brain maps reported; Table 1, figures). All required inclusion criteria are met (I3: social fMRI task; I4: healthy adult sample within 17–65; I5: group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported; I6: acceptable reporting). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating recognition of ‘vitality forms’ (social perception of others’ actions), using a task-based paradigm in healthy adults (N=19, ages 21–29). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses (e.g., how vs what contrast) with voxelwise/cluster-level PFWE-corrected results and MNI coordinates. All required components (introduction, methods, results, discussion) are present in the full text. Therefore it meets I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task activation maps generalizable to healthy adults), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/tables/figures). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social cognition/theory-of-mind in healthy adults (N=46 females, age 18–31). The task probes perception/understanding of others (beliefs, emotions, pain), satisfying the social-related construct. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., B > Ph, E > Ph, Pa > Ph) with cluster-level inference using SnPM, and presents whole-brain maps and tables, meeting whole-brain evidence requirements. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (not just abstract/metadata), so fulltext is complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no restricted age group, etc.). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED in the review.

This paper reports an fMRI study of social processing (peer social-evaluation task) in a sample of healthy participants that includes adult participants (ages up to 22.9). It reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked statistical maps (random-effects analyses) identifying MPFC activations and peak coordinates, and describes PPI connectivity results; whole-brain results are reported and corrected for multiple comparisons. The sample is healthy and contains an adult subgroup within the 17–65 range; although analyses model age continuously across childhood, adolescence, and young adulthood, the reported whole-brain maps derive from the healthy participant group and findings are discussed with respect to adult (young adult) outcomes. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met.

The article reports an fMRI task examining perception/understanding of others (nonverbal dyadic social interactions), using a behavioral rating during scanning (social-related task). Sample comprises healthy adult participants (21 males, ages 23–33). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (multiple contrasts, cluster-level corrected, with tables/coordinates and anatomical localization). Full article sections (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) are present. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social impression formation (perception/understanding of others) using BOLD fMRI during an explicit social task. Participants are healthy adults (N=19, mean age 19.1). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise task contrasts and provides whole-brain coordinates and cluster-corrected results for the functional localizer (form-impression > sequencing) and main task (2×2 ANOVA), satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion, refs) is present. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social perception using passive viewing of biological (point-light) motion versus scrambled motion — a social-related task. It includes a healthy adult group (n=48, ages 20–35) reported separately, meeting the adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise contrasts (biological > scrambled) and Sex×Condition ANOVAs with cluster-corrected thresholds, tables, and figures describing healthy adult activation maps, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion (complete). No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-signal processing in healthy adults (ages 19–28) using tasks involving eye-gaze and self-propelling motion and an implicit mental-inference role-play. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., E–O and S–X; [E–O]+[S–X]) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster correction and provides activation tables and figures. Sample meets the healthy adult age range and results for the healthy group are reported separately. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6; no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social cognition task (third-party punishment/mentalizing), with healthy adult participants (N=26, mean age 26 within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, random-effects whole-brain univariate analyses (GLM) with thresholding (q(FDR)<0.05) and lists Talairach coordinates and figures for activations (e.g., right TPJ, right anterior insula), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. Full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy adults, empirical).

The study reports an fMRI task involving social cognition (viewing traffic campaign videos eliciting mentalizing/empathy), with healthy adult participants (male, ages 19–30) and group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (CV vs NV) reported for the healthy groups (within-group maps and figures). Full article contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6.

No inclusion criteria are satisfied: I3 (use of fMRI during a social task) cannot be confirmed as original data are not reported; I4 (healthy adult sample) is not reported; I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate maps) is not reported; I6 (format of reporting whole-brain results) is not applicable. fulltext_incomplete is set because core article content (methods/results) is missing from the provided text, preventing verification of empirical claims.

The study uses task-based fMRI of face perception (a social-related process) and includes a healthy adult sample (ages 18–37), satisfying I3 and I4. However, the paper does not report a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map that is clearly identified as coming from the healthy adult group alone and generalizable to the healthy adult population. The reported whole-brain results are developmental analyses (age regression across a mixed-age sample) rather than an adult-only whole-brain activation map or contrast. Therefore inclusion criterion I5 is not met. No exclusion criteria were triggered.

This fMRI study investigates attribute framing in social self-evaluation (perception/understanding of self), using task-based functional MRI in healthy adults (ages 19–41). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts are reported (e.g., positive vs negative frame; frame-inconsistent vs frame-consistent), with coordinates and cluster thresholds described, satisfying the requirement for univariate whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy sample. Behavioral and individual-difference analyses are also reported separately for healthy participants. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and is eligible for inclusion.

The study reports an fMRI experiment examining approachability judgments of faces (a social cognition task), clearly meeting I3. It reports data from healthy adult participants (typical adult sample; meets I4). The abstract and text describe group-level task contrasts and activations (left amygdala and frontal gyri) indicating whole-brain, univariate task-evoked results (I5/I6). However, the provided full text appears incomplete (main article content beyond abstract/metadata and references is not available here), so I cannot fully verify reporting details or access tables/figures. Therefore I include the study but flag the full text as incomplete; confidence is moderate.

This paper reports task-based fMRI of a social-emotional paradigm (empathic judgments / emotional egocentricity bias), meeting the review objective. The sample consists of healthy adult participants (right-handed female undergraduates; independent groups across experiments), satisfying the healthy adult criterion. Group-level, univariate whole-brain task analyses are reported: fMRI Experiment 1 used whole-brain exploratory analyses (reported cluster in rSMG), and fMRI Experiment 2 employed independent localizer-based SVC but also performed whole-brain analyses to explore activations outside the VOI; reported group-level contrasts and coordinates are provided. Results are reported for the healthy/control group and are generalizable to healthy adults (not limited to a narrow subgroup). Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met. Note: participants were female undergraduates only (limits generalizability across sexes) but still fall within the eligible healthy adult range. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (dynamic social gestures) in healthy young adults. It reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise task-evoked activation maps and contrasts (TFCE and permutation testing) for the healthy sample with full methods and results. Although the sample range includes one participant aged 16.9 (slightly below 17), the group is described and analyzed as healthy adults (mean age 21.4) and whole-brain healthy-group results are reported and generalizable. The full text is complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an event-related fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=32, age range 18–39) performing a social-related task manipulating collaboration and competition while producing effort. Group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses are reported (SPM results, clusterwise FWE correction; tables/figures provided), linking task regressors (personal utility, collaboration, competition, social position) to voxelwise activations. Behavioral and structural (VBM) results for the healthy sample are presented separately. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy or out-of-range samples, non-empirical) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that probes social cognition: participants (n=20, ages 23–39, healthy) received tactile priming and made judgments about ambiguous social interactions (social coordination). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (ANOVA and post-hoc t-tests) with voxelwise results corrected for multiple comparisons (FDR), figures and tables of activation maps and coordinates (SI, SII, IFG, hippocampus, amygdala, etc.). Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social-related task), I4 (healthy adult sample in age range), I5 (whole-brain, group-level voxelwise task-evoked maps reported and generalized to healthy adults), and I6 (results presented in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

This paper reports voxel-based morphometry (structural MRI) analyses linking grey-matter volume to proneness to moral sentiments in healthy adults (N=63). It does not present task-evoked fMRI whole-brain, group-level univariate activation maps from healthy participants. Although a previously collected SSC-BOLD response from a subgroup (N=29) was used as a predictor in secondary analyses, the article does not provide the required healthy-group whole-brain task activation maps or primary fMRI task results. Therefore it fails inclusion criteria I3 (study uses functional MRI during a social-related task in the reported analyses) and I5 (reports at least one group-level, whole-brain task-evoked statistical map). It meets I4 (healthy adult sample reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are directly triggered by this manuscript.

This is an empirical fMRI study of live verbal social interaction (social communication) using simultaneous scanning of pairs. Participants were healthy adults (22 right-handed women, mean age 27.2), satisfying the sample age and health criteria. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxel-wise second-level t-tests (design-based analyses for talking, listening, imagining) with cluster-corrected thresholds, presented in text, figures, and supplementary tables, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study investigating social evaluation (trustworthiness and attractiveness) using explicit social-judgment tasks on vocal stimuli (meets I3). The sample comprises 44 healthy right-handed adults aged 21–60 (meets I4). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (first- and second-level GLM), cluster-level FWE-corrected results, MNI coordinates, tables and figures (meets I5 and I6). The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants in age range, and it is empirical). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication/empathy in healthy adults (n=27, mean age 34), using task-based fMRI with naturalistic video stimuli assessing social/empathic processing. The paper reports group-level whole-brain random-effects GLM contrasts, conjunction analyses, MNI coordinates, and figures of activations (i.e., univariate voxelwise task-evoked maps) for the healthy participant group. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete.

The study reports an fMRI task explicitly probing social cognition (empathy, Theory of Mind, self–other differentiation), in a sample of healthy adults (15 right-handed males, ages 18–40). Whole-brain, group-level, voxelwise random-effects analyses are reported (ANOVA, contrasts, cluster and voxel thresholds, coordinates, conjunctions, and tables/figures), meeting the requirement for whole-brain task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, and it is empirical fMRI data). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so core article content appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social decision-making (one-shot Prisoner’s Dilemma) in healthy adult participants (n=35 analyzed; mean age 24.6), addressing social cognition, trust, and cooperation. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate GLM analyses and cluster-corrected statistical maps and contrasts (e.g., main effect of SVO, interactions with trust, cooperate vs defect) with figures/tables of activation and coordinates. Full methods, results, and discussion are provided in the supplied full text. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria. Full text appears complete.

This paper reports task-based fMRI during social-related processing (familiar vs unfamiliar faces; affiliation/attachment/social cognition), includes a healthy control group of older adult participants with reported group-level within-group contrasts, and provides whole-brain, voxelwise group activation results (partner>unfamiliar) for the control group with FWE-corrected maps and coordinates. The study therefore meets criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult control group), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate task-evoked maps from controls), and I6 (results reported as coordinates/figures).
