Confidence moderate-high due to clear reporting of healthy-group whole-brain activations; age of control group is reported as mean 64.5 (SD 5.7) which is within the adult range but near the upper bound, but not documented as exclusively outside 17–65, so I4 is considered satisfied.

This empirical fMRI study uses a social task (ultimatum game) and includes a healthy adult group (ages 19–28). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (unfair–fair offers) and one-sample t-tests for each group, with thresholded statistical maps and tables of activations referenced for the healthy adult group. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample 19–28), I5 (group-level whole-brain univariate maps reported for healthy adults), and I6 (results reported as maps/tables described in text). No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social interaction (free online imitation) in healthy adults. Sample: 23 right-handed healthy female adults aged 18–30 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level whole-brain univariate GLM results (contrasts: imitating, being imitated, observation vs rest) with multiple-comparison correction (FWE p<0.05) and provides activation coordinates/tables and figures (Table 1, Fig. 3). Although PPI connectivity analyses are reported, the study also provides task-evoked whole-brain activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6; no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study used natural interpersonal touch (social-related task) in healthy adult participants (I3 and I4 met). However, the paper does not report a group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map (e.g., GLM main-effect or within-group voxelwise contrast). Instead, results are based on group ICA spatial components and component time courses (multivariate decomposition). Per the review criteria, studies that report only ICA/connectivity-type analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map are excluded (E3). Therefore I5 (whole-brain univariate group map) is not met, and the study must be excluded.

This is an empirical fMRI study of face perception (a social-related task) in healthy adult participants (undergraduate sample, mean age ~18.9). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8 second-level GLM) with significant clusters and tables/figures (bilateral fusiform gyrus activations; suprathreshold voxel counts recorded; group activations shown at corrected thresholds). Results for the healthy/control group are reported and generalizable to healthy adults. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study uses task-based fMRI including social-distance trials (names/photos of friends vs acquaintances), satisfying the social-related processing requirement. Participants are healthy adults (N=15; ages 20–28), meeting the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (paired t tests and conjunctions across within-domain contrasts); although these univariate tests yielded no significant clusters at FDR-corrected thresholds, the analyses and results are reported at the group whole-brain level (text and tables/figures for MVPA and univariate results), satisfying the whole-brain reporting criterion. Reporting formats meet acceptable forms. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study includes healthy adult participants and uses task-based fMRI of social processing (I3 and I4 satisfied). However, the reported fMRI results are restricted to ROI-based analyses (beta weights extracted from ROIs) rather than reporting any unmasked, group-level whole-brain voxelwise task activation maps for the healthy group. Therefore exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results) applies, and inclusion criterion I5 (whole-brain task-evoked map) is not met. Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (direct, reflected, and other evaluations across social/academic/physical domains), meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. It includes a healthy adult group (n=19; ages 22–31) with results reported separately and compared to adolescents. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task activation analyses (2×4×3 ANOVA, whole-brain corrected thresholds) and presents clusters/tables (with supplementary within-group analyses referenced), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes adults in required age range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (intro, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social processing (bystander effect) using an unrelated color-naming task while participants viewed emergency scenes, which is a social-related construct (perception/understanding of others; action preparation to help). Sample: healthy adults (N=17, ages 18–27; one excluded for technical failure but group-level results reported), within 17–65. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate voxelwise analyses (parametric GLM, contrasts, cluster-level corrections) with results described and tables/figures of clusters and statistical thresholds. Full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, no connectivity-only, no between-group-only contrasts, participants within age range, empirical fMRI data present). Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social (causal attribution/mentalizing) processing in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–41). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., self>truth, other>truth, conjunction) with whole-brain results and FWE-corrected peaks and coordinate tables. Full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The paper reports an fMRI experiment using a social attribution task (attributing awareness to a cartoon, i.e., social-related processing) in healthy adult participants (N=50, ages 18–49). It provides group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (H trials − E trials) with corrected statistical maps, figures, and Talairach coordinates, satisfying whole-brain evidence. The sample and analyses meet the meta-analysis inclusion criteria and none of the exclusion criteria apply. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (Cyberball exclusion and subsequent social decision-making) reporting task-evoked, group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (multiple whole-brain contrasts and tables of coordinates are reported). Sample consists of healthy adult participants (n=26, mean age 20.7, within 17–65). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (not truncated).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (anticipatory interpersonal touch) in healthy adults. Sample: 16 healthy right-handed adults, ages 20–34 (meets age/sample criterion). The paper reports group-level, voxel-wise whole-brain random-effects analyses and corrected cluster-level inference with coordinates, figures, and tables (meets whole-brain evidence criterion). The task is explicitly social (animate vs. inanimate touch) and uses task-evoked BOLD contrasts. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical) are met. Therefore it satisfies all stated inclusion criteria and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study of self- and other-referential episodic recollection (social cognition/self-understanding), conducted in healthy adult participants (N=18, ages 19–29). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise univariate task contrasts using whole-brain analyses (SPM8), with whole-brain FWE-corrected activations reported outside the mPFC and detailed ROI/SVC results for mPFC—thus providing generalizable healthy-group whole-brain task-evoked maps. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and Tables/Figures. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (self-referential moral processing during intergroup competition) in healthy adults (final N=21, Mage=23.1). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level random-effects analyses with corrected thresholds and tabulated whole-brain results (e.g., Table 2 and clusterwise corrected p<.05), and describes results in text and figures. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps/results), and I6 (whole-brain results presented in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study uses task-based fMRI to examine facial color processing, which is clearly framed as social-information processing (perception/understanding of others and social communication). Participants are healthy adults (N=25, mean age 25.2), meeting the sample age range requirement. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain contrasts (natural-colored face vs. scrambled image) with thresholding and presents group activation maps and peak coordinates (figures and table), satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Although ROI analyses are reported, they were based on and supplemented by whole-brain group contrasts, so the study is not limited to ROI-only results. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria are triggered. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social feedback processing (a social-related task assessing self/other trait evaluation and conformity). Participants were healthy adults (German and Chinese samples) within the adult range, and results for the healthy groups are reported separately. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked activation results (FWE-corrected clusters, contrasts, tables of activations and ROI follow-ups) clearly described in methods and results. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met.

This fMRI study investigates social influence/emotional alignment in interactive one-to-one social communication, using task-based fMRI in healthy adult participants (n=20, mean age ~24). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8; random-effects; cluster-wise FWE correction over the entire brain) with coordinates and figures for activations (anticipation and viewing phases). Full methods, results, and discussion are present in the provided full text. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for task-based social processing in healthy adults and provides whole-brain univariate task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met.

The article reports an fMRI study using a social-related task (first-person video clips of reactive-aggressive, social-positive, and neutral interactions) with a healthy adult sample (n=20 males, mean age 24.6). The paper provides group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts and conjunctions (SPM analyses; thresholding and tables of peak coordinates are reported), fulfilling whole-brain reporting requirements. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not violate any exclusion criteria (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper issues).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing: participants viewed dyadic biological-motion displays manipulating social congruency (typical vs atypical) while undergoing fMRI. Sample: healthy adult participants (10 right-handed males, ages 22–32) — meets age/sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., (atypical upright+inverted) − (typical upright+inverted)), corrected for multiple comparisons, with tables of activated foci and coordinates. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=19, mean age 26.5) using a social-related task (imagining triadic social interactions vs. self/other/iron control), reporting group-level whole-brain univariate contrasts (e.g., triad>iron, conjunctions) with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of activations and PPI analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Hence it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range participants, or non-empirical paper).

This is an fMRI study using an ultimatum game (social interaction task) examining fairness and monetary incentives — fits social-related processing (I3). Sample: 28 healthy adult participants (mean age 25) reported separately — meets I4. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts with voxelwise and clusterwise thresholds and tables/figures of activations (e.g., [unfair>fair], interaction contrasts) — meets I5 and I6. The full text provided includes introduction, methods (participants, task, MRI acquisition, preprocessing, GLM), results, and discussion; supplementary material is referenced but core article content is present, so fulltext_incomplete=false. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This is an fMRI study of socially relevant processing (reaction to opponents' angry vs. neutral facial expressions during an interactive Taylor Aggression Paradigm) in healthy adult participants (32 males, mean age 23.3). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (angry > neutral) with cluster-wise FWE correction and provides tables/figures of results (whole-brain activations for decision and outcome phases). Results are reported for the healthy participant group and are generalizable to healthy adults in the sampled age range. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is present. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6, and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=16, ages 18–25) that used task-based fMRI during a social interaction/competitive game (matching-pennies) manipulating opponent type. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (random-effects second-level one-sample t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction, and provides tables/figures of activated regions and parametric modulation by impression components. The methods, results, and discussion are present in full. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This article investigates fMRI responses during an explicitly social task (impression formation/perception of others varying in moral and financial status), uses a healthy adult sample (20 males, ages 19–31), and reports group-level, univariate whole-brain voxelwise analyses (exploratory whole-brain ANOVA with thresholding; Table 1 and Figures report whole-brain results). Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6. The full text supplied contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext is complete and no exclusion criteria are triggered (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not non-empirical, and healthy adults are within 17–65).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=20 initial; MRI analyses on n=16) investigating implicit theory-of-mind/false-belief processing using task-based fMRI while participants viewed social ‘Sally–Anne’ movies. The task is clearly social (perception/understanding of others' mental states) and uses functional MRI (I3). The sample consists of healthy adults in the target age range (mean age 22.7) with exclusions reported (I4). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts and statistical parametric maps (e.g., belief > photo/map localizer, coordinates and SPMs for implicit contrasts) that are identified as healthy-group effects and reported with thresholds and coordinates (I5). Results are reported in standard coordinate/table and figure form (I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only analysis, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) apply. Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

Full text appears incomplete (only abstract/highlights/metadata provided). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (20 right-handed males, ages 20–28) that investigates socio-emotional processing (empathy/understanding of others) while participants viewed campaign videos. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria are triggered (e.g., the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, reports within-group whole-brain task activations, and participants are within 17–65). Therefore the study should be included in the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task-based fMRI of social-related processing: cross-modal person identity recognition), I4 (healthy adult sample, ages within 20–31, results reported for healthy group). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no whole-brain, group-level univariate task-evoked statistical map reported), I6 (not applicable because qualifying whole-brain results are not provided in tables/figures). This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (perception of biological motion) in healthy adults (n=26 analyzed, ages 18–39). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain analyses relating biological-motion selectivity to social-network measures (with corrected cluster results reported for right pSTS and supplemental figure), satisfying the requirement for a whole-brain task-evoked map generalizable to healthy adults. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (labeling emotional facial expressions—perception and understanding of others). It includes a healthy adult sample (n=50, ages 18–29) and reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (HA>NE, AN>NE, FE>NE) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results and peak coordinates in tables and figures. Whole-brain second-level regression models relating alexithymia to activation are reported; main effects and contrasts for the healthy group are clearly described. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, tables/figures) is provided. No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Therefore the study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis objective.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (ages 20–33) that manipulated a social variable (shared vs unshared viewing with a friend) during task performance and measured task-evoked brain responses. The paper reports group-level univariate task activation results including whole-brain analyses (e.g., whole-brain cluster-corrected activations in DLPFC and precuneus) and ROI-corrected results in reward regions; coordinates and statistical maps are described in tables/figures. All required inclusion criteria for the review are met, and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adults: participants (N=18 healthy females, age 19–28) underwent fMRI while viewing text messages believed to be from a friend or a computer. The task is social-related (perception/understanding of others/ social communication) and uses whole-brain univariate group-level analyses (SPM maps, cluster-level inference) reporting activated clusters (dmPFC, precuneus, TPJ, VOT) — satisfying whole-brain reporting. The full article includes Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, and References and appears complete. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/only connectivity, not between-group-only, age within 17–65, empirical data present). Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met and the study should be INCLUDED in the meta-analysis.

This is an fMRI study of social processing (dynamic social-tie formation in a repeated public-good game) in healthy adult participants (scanned N=25, ages ~22–23). The study uses task-based fMRI during a clearly social/affiliative/other-regarding task (meets I3). The sample is healthy adults within the 17–65 range and results for the healthy group are reported (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, univariate, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked results (parametric modulations, peak MNI coordinates, cluster-level FWE correction, multiple tables and figures) that are clearly identified as coming from the healthy/control group (meets I5 and I6). No exclusion criteria are met (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, patient-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore include.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study of social communication in healthy adult participants (54 right-handed males, age 18–27), meeting the sample inclusion criterion. This is an fMRI study of joint attention (a social communication/process) in healthy adult participants (n=13, mean age 24.85). The full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. This is an fMRI study of social perception using a task that presents dynamic crowds with interactive vs. individual behavior (social interaction perception). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (random-effects ANOVAs) with cluster-corrected results, tables of clusters/coordinates, and whole-brain figures. This is an fMRI study of social interaction/deception (theory-of-mind and social cognition) in healthy adult participants (mean age 24.3, range 21–32). Results are reported as whole-brain analyses (tables and figures) generalizable to the healthy adult sample. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, sample within age range, empirical data present). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=18, ages 18–44) that used a social prediction task (inferring others’ desires vs. rule-following). This is an empirical dfMRI study of face-to-face eye contact (social interaction) using task-based fMRI (tasks A and B) in healthy adult participants (19 pairs, n=38; ages 18–33). This paper reports an fMRI study that directly investigates social attribution (why/how task comparing social vs nonsocial stimuli), uses healthy adult participants (N=19, ages 21–46), and reports group-level whole-brain univariate analyses (why>how contrasts, conjunctions, cluster-corrected t-statistic maps; ROI analyses supplement but whole-brain results are clearly reported). The study employed task-based fMRI (SAMT) probing social-affective modulation of mimicry (affiliation/other-related processing). This is an fMRI study of social processing (social incentive delay task with social reward) in healthy adults (fMRI cohort N=63; ages 20.4–36.6). This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing (social working memory and perspective-taking). This is an fMRI study of gaze following (social attention/communication) in healthy adult participants (N=21, mean age 24.6). The task is clearly social (perception/understanding of others). This is an fMRI study directly examining how people conceptualize actions at different levels of abstraction, recruiting healthy adult participants (N=17; age range 21–46). This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=30, mean age 24.2) that uses face perception tasks (gender identification of angry and happy faces) which are social-related processes (perception/understanding of others). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, non-empirical, or out-of-range age) are met. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

The study reports task-based fMRI during a social/mentalizing task (Prisoner’s Dilemma) in a sample of 164 healthy subjects and describes activation of the mentalizing network and correlations with attachment dimensions, indicating group-level task-evoked whole-brain results. These satisfy inclusion criteria: I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample reported), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked activations reported), and I6 (results described in text/tables). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) appear to apply. However, the provided full text appears incomplete (only highlights/abstract and metadata are shown) and does not explicitly report participant ages or full methods in the supplied content; therefore I set fulltext_incomplete=true and assign moderate confidence.

The study uses task-based fMRI to investigate spontaneous imitation, a social-related process (perception/understanding of others and social communication). Participants are a healthy adult sample (n=37, ages 18–25). The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (parametric modulation, group-level random-effects one-sample t-tests) with cluster-level correction and tables/figures of activations; thus whole-brain healthy-group results are available. Although PPI connectivity is reported, they also provide univariate whole-brain activation maps for the imitation task and correlations with Urge. Full text includes introduction, methods, results and discussion. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria (E2–E6).

Although this paper reports an fMRI social-processing task (viewing/rating parents) with whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts (mother vs. baseline; father vs. baseline) and clearly describes whole-brain results, the participant sample does not constitute a healthy adult group in the target age range. Participants are adolescents (mean age 17.0, range 15.47–18.72) and no separate analysis is reported for a healthy adult subgroup (age 17–65). Therefore inclusion criterion I4 (healthy adult sample) is not met. Full text appears complete. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI social task), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), I6 (results clearly described). Inclusion criterion not met: I4 (healthy adult sample reported separately). No exclusion criteria from the list are strictly met; exclusion is based on failure to satisfy I4.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=33, ages 18–21) that used a task manipulating sociality (social vs non-social scenes) during task-based fMRI and reported group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts (social > non-social; FDR corrected, p<0.05; Table 1 and Figure 1). The paper includes full methods, results, and discussion, and reports ROI analyses in addition to an explicitly described whole-brain activation map. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social reputation processing (a social-related task) conducted in healthy adult participants (N=28, ages 20–24). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked contrasts (positive vs. neutral; negative vs. neutral) with voxelwise thresholding and cluster-level FWE correction and provides peak coordinates (Table 1 and figures). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply. Full text appears complete and adequate for screening.

This article reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (empathy and Theory of Mind) using the EmpaToM paradigm in healthy adult samples (Experiments with N=25, 65, 178; ages reported within 17–65). The paper presents group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task contrasts (emotionally negative > neutral; ToM > nonToM) with statistical thresholds and activation peak tables/coordinates, and describes random-effects analyses and resting-state connectivity. Behavioral and neural results for the healthy groups are reported separately. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults using a social gaze-following task with political in-group/out-group stimuli (social-related processing). Sample: 28 healthy adults aged 18–36, reported separately and meeting the age range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (incongruent > congruent), thresholding, cluster correction, and tables/figures with reported coordinates, suitable as whole-brain activation maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, not only between-group contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text provided appears complete (methods, results, discussion).

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study using a validated social (Theory of Mind) task (moving-triangles animations), with a healthy adult sample (N=20; ages 24–64) within the 17–65 range. The authors report group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., ToM > R, ToM > Baseline) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level inference, and provide peak coordinates and figures. All required inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical study). Full text is complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This study uses fMRI in healthy adults and reports whole-brain task activation maps, but the task is emotional picture viewing (negative/positive/neutral IAPS) focused on emotion processing rather than an explicit social-related task/construct. Although the authors discuss dmPFC (a region implicated in social cognition) and stimuli sometimes include people, the experimental manipulation targets negative emotion processing and not clearly a social construct such as affiliation, social communication, or perception/understanding of others. Therefore inclusion criterion I3 (social-related task) is not met. Inclusion criteria met: I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps reported), I6 (whole-brain results clearly described). No exclusion criteria apply (none of E2–E6 are met). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study that investigates empathy for pain as modulated by experimentally induced (ingroup/outgroup) social categories — a social-related task (perception/understanding of others). The sample consists of 30 healthy adult participants (ages 18–35), meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, voxelwise SPM analyses (main effect of pain, main effect of condition, pain×condition interaction) with cluster-level and FWE-corrected results and tables described in the text, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Results are presented for the healthy/control group and are generalizable to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, ages within range, and it is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=15, mean age 23.6) that used task-based functional MRI while participants viewed social interactions (violent dyadic interactions) and manipulated attentional focus—this addresses social perception/understanding of others. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., all conditions vs baseline; focus on aggressor vs victim) with statistical maps, cluster correction, and coordinates/figures, satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. All inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6 are met, and no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (includes introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an fMRI study of social-related processing (fiction passages varying Social vs Non-social; relates to Theory of Mind), with a healthy adult sample (N=26, ages 19–26) and behavioral ToM measures. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects contrasts (e.g., Social>Non-social and Vivid>Abstract) with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates (Table 1), satisfying whole-brain univariate reporting. Methods, results, and discussion are present in the full text. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants are within 17–65, and it is empirical). Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults that directly investigates social-related processing. The task included implicit social stimuli (pictures depicting humans) and self-referential judgments; the sample comprised 28 healthy adults aged 30–50. The authors report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise GLM analyses (ANOVA and direct contrasts/conjunctions) with results thresholded and reported (FDR-corrected; cluster extent) and described in text/tables/figures. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates none of the exclusion criteria. Full text content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, References) is present and sufficient for screening.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social task (Cyberball social exclusion) with healthy adult participants (unmarried university students), and reports group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses (exclusion vs inclusion) with coordinates/tables and whole-brain interaction and two-sample whole-brain comparisons. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies all relevant inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and violates no exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social perception (racial in-group/out-group disgust perception) using a passive face-viewing task, which qualifies as social-related processing. Participants were healthy adults (n=26 after exclusions; mean age 21.2), satisfying the sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (2×2 repeated-measures ANOVA; corrected whole-brain clusters, coordinates, tables, and figures) including the critical interaction contrast ((disgusted out-group–neutral out-group)–(disgusted in-group–neutral in-group)). Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included in the meta-analysis.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (processing agentic vs. communal trait words) using a valence classification task. Participants were healthy adult university students (age range 18–25). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain voxelwise analyses (SPM8; conjunction and pairwise contrasts; AlphaSim-corrected results) with coordinates and figures/tables of activations/deactivations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, participants within age range, empirical data present). Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis.

This report is an empirical fMRI study of social-communicative processing (understanding Naming vs. Requesting speech acts). It used task-based functional MRI in healthy adult participants (n=18 analyzed; ages 18–41), meeting the age/sample requirement. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects analyses (voxelwise contrasts, FDR-corrected) and tables/figures of activations, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range sample, or non-empirical) apply. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be included.

This is an empirical hyperscanning fMRI study of face-to-face social interaction (mutual gaze and joint attention) in healthy adult participants (mean ages ~21–23). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task analyses (GLM/SPM) with voxelwise results and tables of coordinates and cluster-level statistics (FWE-corrected), including contrasts such as MG2–MG1 and JA-related activations. Behavioral–neural correlations and ROI checks are supplementary but whole-brain task maps are clearly reported. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI during social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

This is an empirical fMRI study that directly investigates social-related processing (dynamic social gestures) in healthy adults using a task contrasting social vs nonsocial gestures. The methods report group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task-evoked analyses (FLAME, cluster correction) with reported coordinates and figures, and results are provided for the healthy participant group (N=20, mean age 21.4, range 16.9–25.7). Although one participant is reported as age 16.9 (just below 17), the sample is described and analyzed as a healthy young adult group and group-level whole-brain results are reported, so inclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete.

This paper reports an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=59–60, mean age ~20) that used a social task probing interpersonal trust/distrust (control-of-trust/distrust), satisfying the review focus on social-related processing. The manuscript presents whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation contrasts (e.g., trust>age, distrust>age, trust+distrust>age) with FWE-corrected thresholds and tables/figures of results and reports exploratory connectivity analyses; results are clearly reported for the healthy sample. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult participants (n=26; mean age 28.7) using task-based paradigms probing social perception and cognition (face-viewing, person-judgment), satisfying the review objective. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects parametric analyses (e.g., Fig. S1, Table S4) mapping target popularity effects across the brain, and describes these whole-brain results in the text and supplemental tables, meeting the whole-brain evidence requirement. ROI analyses are present but whole-brain results are also reported. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply.

This fMRI study directly investigates social cognition (empathic concern/compassion) using an active task with empathy-evoking film clips and contextual framing, satisfying the review objective. Sample: 26 healthy adult participants (age mean 30.3, range within 17–65) — meets the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (e.g., sad vs neutral context, multisensory > unisensory) with cluster-level FWE-corrected results presented in tables and figures, fulfilling whole-brain evidence requirements. Whole-brain results are described in text, tables, and figures (Supplementary tables referenced), so coordinate/table/figure reporting is acceptable. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, includes healthy-group task maps). Full text appears complete.

This is an fMRI study of social interaction in healthy adults that reports whole-brain, group-level task activation contrasts. The task directly probes social communication/interaction (perceived live vs recorded speech). Sample: healthy adult participants (n=29, ages 18–27) with results reported for the healthy group. Whole-brain contrasts (Live > Social; Social > Standard) are reported, thresholded and cluster-corrected, with figures/tables and region coordinates; individual-subject mentalizing localizer and group-level maps are described. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met. Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (mentalizing about others’ mental states) using task-based fMRI in healthy adults (N=20, ages 18–27). The paper reports whole-brain group-level analyses (searchlight MVPA results combined via one-sample t tests, network-level analyses, and parallel univariate whole-brain mapping with cluster correction; Tables S2/S3 and figures display whole-brain results), satisfying requirements for whole-brain task-evoked maps. The task probes perception/understanding of others, and healthy adult group results are reported and generalizable. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion; supplementary figures/tables are referenced. No exclusion criteria are met.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI study of social learning about others’ generosity (social cognition), with healthy adult participants (final N=26, ages 19–37). It includes full methods, MRI acquisition/preprocessing, behavioral and whole-brain voxelwise group-level univariate analyses (conjunctions, contrasts, cluster-corrected maps, peak coordinates, and tables/figures) clearly reported for the healthy group. The content appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Therefore the study meets all required inclusion criteria (I3, I4, I5, I6) and is appropriate for inclusion.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). From available text: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task — live eye contact) is satisfied. However I4 (sample: healthy adult participants 17–65) is not verifiable from the provided content, and I5 (reporting a group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for healthy controls) is not reported in the abstract. Because core information needed to confirm key inclusion criteria is missing, the study is excluded pending a complete full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be confirmed from the available content.

Full text appears incomplete (only title/abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an rt-fMRI+EEG neurofeedback study targeting social communication and right pSTS, satisfying I3 (fMRI during social-related task). However the provided content does not report participant sample details (cannot confirm healthy adults 17–65; I4 not met) nor present any group-level, whole-brain univariate task activation maps for a healthy group (I5 not met). Cannot determine whether results are ROI-only or include whole-brain maps. Because core article content (methods, participants, group whole-brain results) is missing, the study cannot be confirmed to meet all inclusion criteria and is excluded pending full text. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be definitively applied from available info.

This is an fMRI study of affective theory-of-mind (social cognition) using a task manipulating emotional facial expressions during cartoon stories. The sample comprises healthy adult participants (N=21 analyzed; mean age ~23.7) within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (one-sample t-tests, whole-brain contrasts, tables of peak coordinates and figures) in the healthy sample, and also presents results in text/tables/figures. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and violates no exclusion criteria.

The study reports a task-based fMRI experiment probing social-related processing (effects of receiving cognitively and emotionally empathic comments) in healthy adult participants (N=20, mean age 26). The paper provides whole-brain, group-level univariate activation results (voxelwise contrasts; FWE-corrected clusters and tables of activations are reported), not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses. The full text includes Introduction, Methods (participants, task, fMRI acquisition and whole-brain analysis), Results, and Discussion, so the full text appears complete. Therefore inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply.

This study reports an fMRI experiment of social processing (perception of others’ facial expressions) in healthy adult participants (n=24, mean age 25.2), satisfying I3 and I4. The authors performed first-level and mixed-effects group-level univariate analyses (parameter estimate maps registered to MNI) and report a group-level faces>scrambled-faces localiser contrast used to define ROIs, which constitutes whole-brain, group-level task-evoked univariate results generalizable to healthy adults (I5). The manuscript contains full Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, and the text describes whole-brain results (I6 acceptable). No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only reporting, connectivity-only analyses, patient-only samples, or non-empirical paper) are met. Full text appears complete. Therefore the study should be INCLUDED.

This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-evaluative task (watching positive, negative, neutral social videos) in a healthy adult sample (N=37, mean age 24.8). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate contrasts (positive>neutral, negative>neutral, conjunction) with family-wise error corrected results and cluster coordinates in tables and figures, satisfying the whole-brain evidence requirement. Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (race perception and trustworthiness evaluations) using a task involving face perception and trustworthiness ratings, satisfying the social-related task requirement. Participants were 30 healthy right-handed White adults aged 18–29, meeting the healthy adult sample criterion. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate voxelwise analyses (e.g., Black>White contrast, second-level covariate analyses) with cluster-thresholding and tables of peak coordinates, fulfilling the whole-brain evidence requirement; results are presented in tables/figures and described in text (acceptable reporting per I6). Although the paper also reports PPI connectivity analyses, these supplement rather than replace whole-brain task activation maps. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete with Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion.

This fMRI study investigates social cognition (linking person perception and person knowledge) using a task where participants view bodies or names paired with trait or neutral statements. It reports behavioral and group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (main effects and interaction contrasts) with voxelwise thresholds and tables of coordinates, and includes healthy adult participants (n=21, mean age 24.6). Whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps/contrasts (e.g., Bodies>Names, Traits>Neutral, interaction) are clearly described and generalizable to healthy adults. Therefore it satisfies all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition (theory of mind) using a task with social and non-social stories. Participants were healthy adults (N=24, mean age 25.7). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects univariate analyses (voxel-wise threshold P<0.001, cluster-wise FWE-corrected results shown in Tables 2–3) and ROI/MVPA analyses; whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy sample are described. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so full text appears complete. Thus all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) it uses fMRI during social-related tasks (social judgment of dominance and trustworthiness); (I4) sample comprises healthy adults aged 21–43 (n=23); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrast (Social Judgment > Perceptual Judgment) with FWE-corrected cluster results and a table of coordinates; (I6) whole-brain results are presented in tables and figures and clearly described. No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI examining social-related processing (meaning vs physical judgments of symbolic artifacts), uses a healthy adult sample (25 right-handed adults, mean age 24), and reports group-level whole-brain, voxelwise univariate results (random-effects SPM8 analyses with thresholding and tables/figures of activations and peak coordinates). The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an fMRI study using the Cyberball (ball-toss) social interaction task (social reward/affiliation), conducted in healthy adult participants (final N=31; ages ~21). The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation results with voxelwise coordinates and cluster-level inference (voxel p<0.005, cluster FWE p<0.05) for contrasts relevant to social interaction. Full article includes introduction, methods, results, discussion, and references. It is not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, and reports healthy-group whole-brain task effects generalizable to healthy adults. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria and violates no exclusion criteria.

This task-state fMRI study focuses on self-referential processing (a social-related construct), but it does not report a group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked activation map for healthy adults. Instead, analyses are ROI-based and seed-based voxel-level functional connectivity (task-state connectivity) and between-group connectivity differences. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (task fMRI addressing self-referential/social processing). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 (participant ages for healthy/control group are not provided to confirm they fall within 17–65), I5 (no group-level univariate whole-brain task activation map for the healthy/control group), I6 (not applicable because I5 not satisfied). Exclusion criteria met: E3 (study reports only seed-/connectivity-based analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map) and E4 (the paper emphasizes between-group connectivity differences and lacks an accompanying unmasked whole-brain healthy-group task effect). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so fulltext_incomplete=false.

The study reports task-based fMRI of a clearly social paradigm (socially-induced cognitive emotion regulation by a psychotherapist), using healthy adult participants (female, ages 22–32). Group-level, whole-brain univariate contrasts are reported (e.g., Social-Reg > Social-Look) with cluster-wise FWE correction, tables and coordinates, and behavioral correlations; methods, results and discussion are present in the full text. This meets inclusion for social-related fMRI task (I3), healthy adult sample (I4), and whole-brain group-level task activation maps reported (I5,I6). No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range ages, or non-empirical) apply. Full text appears complete.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review objective. It uses task-based fMRI during a social interaction paradigm (Taylor Aggression Paradigm) addressing social-emotional processing (retaliation/provocation) (I3). The sample consists of healthy adult participants (N=15; mean age 22.3), within the 17–65 range (I4). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (random-effects group maps, Talairach coordinates, figures, and cluster-corrected thresholds) clearly identified as coming from the healthy participant group (I5). Whole-brain results are provided in tables of coordinates and figures (I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical study limitations). The full text provided includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. Note: sample size is small and limited to young males, a limitation for generalizability but not an exclusion under the stated criteria.

The abstract and highlights indicate the study used fMRI during an interactive mentalizing (prisoner’s dilemma) paradigm—a social cognition task—and reports neural activation findings (bilateral temporal pole, precunei, right middle/superior frontal gyri) in a healthy adult sample (n=195 overall, fMRI subgroup n=163). These indicate group-level, task-evoked voxelwise results consistent with whole-brain univariate analyses typical for NeuroImage reports. Therefore the study appears to meet inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult participants), and I5 (whole-brain task-evoked results). However, the provided “full text” is incomplete (only highlights, abstract, and references are present), so I cannot fully verify that statistical maps are unmasked, clearly identified as healthy-group maps, or that all reporting conventions meet I5/I6. Due to that uncertainty I set fulltext_incomplete=true and a moderate confidence score.

This is an empirical fMRI study of social processing (charitable giving, empathy, perspective taking) in healthy adults (N=33; ages 20–34). The paper reports task-based fMRI with whole-brain analyses: group-level GLMs and random-effects contrasts (e.g., EmpaToM contrasts used to define voxels, univariate GLM results reported including a significant visual-cortex cluster for low>high donations), and multiple whole-brain, voxelwise MVPA/SVR/searchlight results and group-level statistics. Results are reported as group-level maps/tables and described in the text and tables. Thus it meets inclusion I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked analyses are reported), and I6 (results presented in text/tables). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not between-group-only, ages within range, empirical data present). Full text appears complete (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

Excluded because the study reports only functional connectivity / network analyses during task and rest and does not present any group-level univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps for the healthy group. Exclusion criteria met: E3 (connectivity-only analyses without a healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Inclusion criteria met: I3 (used fMRI with an emotion face matching task that falls under social perception/understanding of others) and I4 (healthy adult sample from the Human Connectome Project). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (no reported group-level, univariate whole-brain task activation maps for the healthy/control group). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion). Therefore EXCLUDED.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (N=178, mean age 40.9 within 17–65). It uses a social cognition task (EmpaToM) manipulating empathy and Theory of Mind, and presents group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (emotional vs neutral videos; ToM vs non-ToM questions/videos) with statistical maps/coordinate tables and results generalizable to the healthy group. Methods, results, and discussion are fully reported in the full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (group-level whole-brain task-evoked maps), and I6 (whole-brain results reported in figures/tables). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text appears complete.

Full text appears incomplete (only highlights, abstract, abbreviations, keywords, and references provided). Inclusion I3 (fMRI during a social task: cooperation vs. competition) is met based on the abstract. However, I4 (explicit sample details confirming healthy adult participants aged 17–65) is not verifiable from the provided content. I5 (reporting of at least one group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical map for the healthy/control group) cannot be confirmed — the abstract mentions univariate analyses but does not provide or state whole-brain group-level maps or coordinate tables. I6 (acceptable reporting of whole-brain results in tables/figures/supplement) also cannot be verified. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are clearly met based on the available text. Because core methods/results and participant details are missing, I must exclude pending a complete full text.

Full text is incomplete (only abstract/metadata provided). Abstract indicates an fMRI social-learning task (I3 met). However the report does not provide participant demographics or specify that the sample consists of healthy adults aged 17–65 (I4 not verifiable) and does not provide the full methods/results needed to confirm that at least one group-level, univariate whole-brain task activation map for the healthy group is reported (I5 not verifiable). Because the full text (methods and results) is unavailable, I cannot confirm compliance with I4 and I5 required for inclusion. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) can be positively identified from the abstract alone. Recommend obtaining the full text to reassess inclusion.

This is an fMRI study of social impression updating (a social cognitive task involving perception/understanding of others), with a healthy adult sample (N=21, ages 18–31). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., L2>F3 contrasts, 2×4 ANOVA, corrected thresholds using AlphaSim) with tables/figures of activations and extracted parameter estimates. Results are not limited to ROI or connectivity-only analyses, and healthy-group whole-brain effects are clearly reported and generalizable to adults in the target age range. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion.

This is an fMRI study of Theory of Mind (REMICS task) directly probing social cognition/mentalizing. Participants: 19 healthy adults age 20–53 (within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain random-effects analyses (one-sample t-tests) with voxelwise thresholds and cluster-level correction, and provides tables of activation coordinates and figures. Thus it provides univariate whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, out-of-range ages) apply. This is an original fMRI study of social processing (modified Cyberball task combining social exclusion and performance evaluation) in healthy adults (n=40, mean age 27.8). This is an empirical fMRI study using a social role judgment task (self, friend, celebrity) that probes perception/understanding of self and others (social-related processing). Sample: 37 healthy adult males (mean age 22.9), which falls within the 17–65 range. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts (self vs. celebrity; friend vs. celebrity) with voxelwise statistics and FDR correction, and provides peak coordinates and tables/figures. Thus it meets I3 (fMRI social task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables reported). No exclusion criteria are met. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion, and appears complete.

The full text describes an fMRI study using an iterated prisoner's dilemma social decision-making task (meets I3). Sample: 20 healthy adult participants aged 23–38, reported as healthy and screened (meets I4). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., conjunction of task>control, COMP>COOP) with cluster-level correction and peak coordinates, and extracts percent-signal-change from significant clusters (meets I5 and I6). The manuscript includes Introduction, Methods (behavioral and fMRI acquisition/preprocessing/GLM), Results (behavioral, whole-brain, time-course, gPPI), and Discussion, so the provided full text appears complete. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: results are not ROI-only, not limited to connectivity or resting-state only, not only between-group contrasts, participants are within the 17–65 range, and this is an empirical fMRI study. Therefore INCLUDE for the review of fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

The study reports an empirical task-based fMRI experiment directly comparing social vs. non-social stimuli with healthy adult participants (ages 23–50) and uses whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses. Methods and results include a group-level social > non-social contrast with voxelwise thresholds and FDR correction, tables/figures of cluster results, and ROI/whole-brain conjunction analyses. The sample is healthy adults (n=14 analyzed), and whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps (group contrasts) are clearly reported. Full text contains introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based fMRI during a social-related emotion perception task (perception/understanding of others via facial and prosodic cues), with healthy adult participants within the 17–65 range. The paper provides group-level, whole-brain, voxelwise task analyses (repeated-measures ANOVA and paired t-tests) with PFWE-corrected results, cluster tables and coordinates, and ROI analyses. Full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Therefore it satisfies I3, I4, I5, and I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) are met. Full text appears complete.

However the full text is not available to confirm critical eligibility requirements: participant characteristics (age range and health status) to satisfy I4 and whether group-level, univariate whole-brain voxelwise task maps are reported to satisfy I5/I6. This paper reports an fMRI study of social-related processing (self-evaluation and endorsement of others’ evaluations) using a task-based design in healthy adults. The sample consists of healthy adults (n=31, ages 19–24). The manuscript presents group-level, whole-brain univariate task contrasts and a whole-brain multiple regression with self-esteem as regressor, with results reported in tables of coordinates and thresholded maps (voxel-wise p<0.001, cluster-level FWE-corrected p<0.05). Psychophysiological interaction (PPI) analyses are additional connectivity analyses but do not replace the whole-brain task activations. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

This is an fMRI study of social evaluation in healthy adults (meets I3 and I4), but the analyses were restricted to predefined ROIs (search regions restricted to amygdala, insula, IFG, ACC, thalamus, caudate, mOFC) and no unmasked whole-brain (voxelwise) group-level task activation map is reported. Therefore it fails inclusion criterion I5 and meets exclusion criterion E2 (ROI-only analyses with no whole-brain results). Full text appears complete.

Includes an explicit social cognition task (social interaction vs. random movement) using task fMRI; participants are healthy adults drawn from HCP and UCLA datasets with ages within 21–50 (within 17–65 range); the paper reports group-level, voxel-wise task activation analyses and displays activation maps (e.g., Figure 1 and Supplementary figures) derived from healthy/control participants, satisfying whole-brain reporting requirements. The study is empirical and not limited to ROI/connectivity-only outcomes. Therefore it meets I3, I4, I5, and I6 and does not meet any exclusion criteria.

Exclusion applied: E5 — the study sample consists of adolescents (ages 14–18, M=16.3) and does not report a separate healthy adult subgroup (17–65). Inclusion criteria met: I3 — the study uses task-based fMRI of a social-related task (social-reward/peer feedback); I6 — whole-brain results are reported in text/figures/tables (group-level contrasts are presented). Inclusion criteria not met: I4 — no healthy adult participant group (17–65) is analyzed/reported separately; I5 — although group-level whole-brain maps are reported, they are from an adolescent sample and are not clearly generalizable to a healthy adult population. Full text completeness: fulltext_incomplete=false. Because the review seeks fMRI evidence generalizable to healthy adults and this study reports only an adolescent healthy sample without an adult subgroup, it must be excluded under E5.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=55, mean age 24.9) using a social-related task (extended Hariri face/scene matching with erotic and fearful social scenes), satisfying the review objective. The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (e.g., erotic>neutral, fearful>neutral, erotic>fearful) with whole-brain FWE-corrected results and ROI analyses; figures and tables of results are presented. All inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6). No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, age out-of-range, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (N=22, mean age 24.4) that uses task-based fMRI during social-cognitive tasks (mind perception and gaze cueing). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (parametric regressors, FLAME1), cluster-level corrected results and coordinates (tables/figures) identifying vmPFC and other regions; results are described as whole-brain maps and coordinate tables. The sample falls within the 17–65 age range and results for the healthy group are reported. Full article text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met (I3,I4,I5,I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This fMRI study examines maternal neural responses to their own child’s facial emotions (a social/attachment-related task), meeting the social-processing domain. It includes a healthy adult control group (mothers without early-life maltreatment) reported separately. The paper reports whole-brain, group-level univariate task activation results (e.g., familiarity own>unknown in CON: medial frontal gyrus, pFWE<0.001) as well as other whole-brain and ROI analyses, satisfying the requirement for whole-brain healthy-group task-evoked maps. The full text contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are met; no exclusion criteria apply. Confidence is high given clear within-group whole-brain reporting for the healthy control group.

The full text reports an empirical fMRI task explicitly probing social-related processing (recall of self- and other-relationship episodes), includes a healthy adult sample (n=35; diagnostic interview confirmed no mental disorders), and presents group-level whole-brain voxelwise task contrasts (self-relevant>control, other>control) with FDR correction and clusterwise inference. Results are reported in tables and figures and are generalizable to a healthy adult group. The manuscript contains Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion sections, so the full text is complete for screening. Therefore all inclusion criteria are met and no exclusion criteria apply.

This is a task-based fMRI study of social perception (integration of facial and vocal emotional expressions), conducted in healthy adults (n=24, mean age 26). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain univariate analyses (random-effects, FWE-corrected maps and coordinates) demonstrating bimodal > unimodal effects (rpSTS) and congruency effects; results and statistical thresholds are described and tables/coordinates provided. The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion. Thus it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample 17–65), I5 (whole-brain group-level task-evoked maps), and I6 (coordinates/tables described). No exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis. It uses fMRI during a social cognition task (face-based trustworthiness judgments with feedback), satisfying I3. It reports a healthy younger adult group (ages 20–33), satisfying I4 (healthy adults 17–65 present and reported separately). The paper presents group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses (ANOVA and whole-brain results, with reported clusters and a Supplementary Table 2), satisfying I5; statistical thresholds and cluster-level FWE correction are described. Whole-brain results are presented in tables/figures (coordinates and cluster peaks), satisfying I6. No exclusion criteria (E2–E6) apply: the study is not ROI-only, not connectivity- or resting-state-only, includes an analysable healthy adult group within 17–65, and is empirical with original fMRI data. Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion included).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social cognition that meets all inclusion criteria. It used task-based fMRI while participants made judgments about others’ mental states (social-related task), satisfying I3. The sample consists of healthy adults (N=28 after one exclusion; ages 18–22), satisfying I4. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain analyses: a searchlight representational similarity analysis and voxelwise univariate repetition suppression analyses with permutation TFCE correction, reporting peak coordinates and clusters (medial PFC, posterior precuneus), satisfying I5 and I6 (results presented as corrected maps and coordinates/figures). The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion, so fulltext_incomplete is false. No exclusion criteria apply.

This is an empirical fMRI study using an iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma (a social decision-making task) performed during functional MRI, with analyses and results reported for a healthy adult sample. Sample: 20 healthy male adults (age range 21–37), meeting the healthy adult criterion. Whole-brain, group-level univariate analyses are reported (one-sample t tests, flexible factorial analyses; FWE cluster-corrected maps and tables of cluster activations are presented). Results are described in text, tables, and figures. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (e.g., ROI-only, connectivity-only, non-healthy sample, non-empirical) apply. Therefore the article meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adults (n≈300 randomized; final analytic samples reported) using a social-interaction task (iterated Prisoner’s Dilemma) performed during BOLD fMRI, meeting the review’s social-related task requirement. The sample consists of healthy adults aged 18–22 (within 17–65). The paper reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked analyses (thresholding, cluster correction, whole-brain results and coordinates described in text and tables; analyses reported for healthy/placebo and treatment groups and subgroup analyses), satisfying whole-brain evidence requirements. Full article content (Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion) is present. No exclusion criteria (ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only without whole-brain healthy maps, out-of-range age, or non-empirical paper) are met.

This is an empirical fMRI study in healthy adult males (ages 18–35) using a social provocation task (modified Taylor Aggression Paradigm) that probes social processing (provocation, decision-making about another person). The paper reports group-level, whole-brain, univariate task-evoked contrasts (high vs low provocation) with FWEc cluster correction and provides MNI coordinates and figures for these contrasts, clearly attributable to the healthy participant sample. Methods, results, and discussion are present in full text. Therefore it meets inclusion criteria I3 (social-related fMRI task), I4 (healthy adult sample), I5 (whole-brain group-level univariate task maps), and I6 (results reported in tables/figures/text). No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity/resting-state-only, not exclusively between-group contrasts, and participants are within the age range). Full text appears complete for screening purposes.

Meets all inclusion criteria: (I3) uses task-based dual-fMRI hyperscanning during an interactive social task (cooperation/competition, social exchange); (I4) healthy adult sample (N=44, mean age 22.37, ages within 17–65); (I5) reports group-level, whole-brain univariate task-evoked analyses (GLM, FLAME random-effects, non-parametric permutation correction) with tables/figures of voxelwise results; (I6) whole-brain results are reported as tables of coordinates and whole-brain t-maps. No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, not between-group-only contrasts, not outside age range, and is empirical). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion, references).
