This is an empirical fMRI study using a social-related task (face perception/recognition — ‘Perception and Understanding of Others’), with healthy adult participants (Experiment 1: N=20, mean age ~25; additional behavioral samples also healthy). The paper reports group-level fMRI analyses including a group-level univariate localizer contrast (faces vs scrambled; n=83) used to define ROIs and describes mixed-effects (FLAME) group analyses registered to MNI space, satisfying the requirement for a group-level, task-evoked whole-brain map generalizable to healthy adults. Results and methods are fully reported (introduction, methods, results, discussion), so full text appears complete. Therefore all relevant inclusion criteria are met (I3, I4, I5, I6) and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets all inclusion criteria for the review: I3 — it uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (live bidirectional conversation contrasting human–human and human–robot interactions, addressing social communication/mentalizing/social motivation); I4 — includes a healthy adult sample (n=21 after exclusions; mean age 25.8, within 17–65); I5 — reports group-level, whole-brain univariate voxelwise task contrasts (HHI vs HRI) analyzed with SPM and thresholded at p<0.05 FDR cluster-level, with figures and NeuroVault/OpenNeuro data shared; I6 — whole-brain results are clearly described in text and figures (and shared online). No exclusion criteria apply (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not restricted to non-healthy or out-of-range ages, not non-empirical). Full text appears complete (contains Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion).

The study reports task-based fMRI of social cognition (empathy toward human vs robot), using healthy adult participants (n=26, ages 18–27). It includes group-level whole-brain random-effects analyses (cluster-corrected and uncorrected maps), reports whole-brain results in text/figures/tables, and shares maps on NeuroVault/OSF. The full article (intro, methods, results, discussion) is provided. Thus it meets all inclusion criteria for fMRI studies of social processing in healthy adults.

This study reports task-based fMRI in a healthy adult sample (n=20, ages 22–35) using a social-communication paradigm (naturalistic narrative with co-speech gestures). The paper provides group-level, voxelwise whole-brain task contrasts (e.g., low_ID > high_ID; speech > gestures+speech; gestures+speech > speech) with tables of activation peaks, cluster extents, and thresholding procedures, clearly attributable to the healthy participant group. Full article text (intro, methods, results, discussion) is available. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not connectivity-only, not limited to between-group contrasts, participants are within 17–65, and it is empirical). Therefore the study meets inclusion criteria for the review.

This study uses fMRI with a social task (cyberball) and includes a healthy adult control group, so inclusion criteria I3 and I4 are met. However, the full text reports primarily between-group contrasts (BPD vs NSSI, conjunctions vs HC) and does not present an unmasked, whole-brain, group-level task activation map specifically for the healthy control group (no HC within-group whole-brain task effect is reported). Therefore it violates exclusion criterion E4 (only between-group contrasts reported without an accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task effect). Inclusion criteria not met: I5 (healthy-group whole-brain map).

The study meets all inclusion criteria for the meta-analysis: (I3) It uses task-based fMRI during a social-related task (animacy perception/perception of others); (I4) samples healthy adult participants (ages reported 19–36, healthy, N=111 overall, N≈36 included in fMRI analyses); (I5) reports group-level, univariate whole-brain task-evoked statistical maps and contrasts (whole-brain conjunctions and FWE-corrected voxelwise results, reported in figures and tables); (I6) whole-brain results are presented in figures/tables and described in text. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, connectivity-only, between-group-only, out-of-range age-only, or non-empirical issues). Full text appears complete (introduction, methods, results, discussion present).

This is an empirical fMRI study of social-related processing: it includes multiple social cognition tasks (false belief, animacy/intentional triangles, eyes intention, trustworthiness, face and vocalization tasks) that probe perception/understanding of others. Sample: 78 healthy adults (age 18–40), meeting the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, whole-brain random-effects voxelwise analyses (RFX) with maps thresholded at p<0.05 FWE and provides Tables/figures of whole-brain results and NeuroVault availability; thus it provides univariate whole-brain task-evoked maps for the healthy group. The full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion. Therefore all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 are satisfied and no exclusion criteria apply.

This study meets inclusion criteria: I3 (task-based fMRI of social processing—observation of dynamic facial expressions, a social communication/perception task), I4 (healthy adult sample: n=51, ages within 17–65), I5 (reports group-level whole-brain univariate analyses—random-effects one-sample t-tests and ANOVAs with voxel-wise family-wise error correction), and I6 (whole-brain results clearly described in text, with tables/figures and coordinates). The full text includes introduction, methods, results, and discussion and appears complete. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only; not connectivity/resting-state only; includes healthy-group whole-brain task activations).

Instead, the paper presents ROI-based functional connectivity and graph-theoretical analyses using the Power-264 atlas. Inclusion criteria met: I3 (fMRI during a social-related task: vocal emotional processing/social communication) and I4 (healthy adult sample, ages 20–35). Inclusion criterion not met: I5 (no whole-brain voxelwise task activation map reported). Exclusion criteria met: E2 (reports only ROI/atlas-based connectivity analyses with no whole-brain results) and E3 (reports connectivity/graph-theory analyses without accompanying healthy-group whole-brain task activation map). Full text appears complete (methods, results, discussion present).

This paper reports an fMRI study using social tasks (take-advice game and trust game) clearly probing social cognition/trust (meets I3). Sample comprises 31 healthy adult participants (age mean 24.3), meeting I4. The manuscript reports group-level, whole-brain univariate results (voxel- and cluster-level FWE thresholds, contrasts such as honesty>dishonesty, value contrasts, and Supplementary Tables with coordinates), satisfying I5 and I6. The full text provided includes Introduction, Methods (subjects, task, imaging acquisition/preprocessing, GLMs), Results, Discussion, and References, so core content is present and complete. No exclusion criteria apply (no ROI-only, no resting-state-only, no between-group-only contrasts, and participants are within age range). Therefore the study should be INCLUDED for the meta-analysis of fMRI studies of social-related processing in healthy adults.

The study uses task-based fast fMRI to compare vocal (socially relevant) versus non-vocal sounds, addressing social communication/perception of others (I3). Participants are healthy adults within the 17–65 range (Experiment 1: n=13, mean age ~26.6; Experiment 2: n=18, mean age ~23.1), satisfying sample criterion (I4). The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain activation contrasts (vocal > non-vocal) with thresholding and coordinates/figures (Fig.1 and described GLM results), providing whole-brain univariate task-evoked maps generalizable to healthy adults (I5/I6). Full text includes Introduction, Methods, Results, and Discussion; not truncated. No exclusion criteria are met (e.g., this is not ROI-only, not resting-state only, and not non-empirical). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria for the review.

This paper reports task-based functional MRI during observation of social (interpersonal) touch scenes (MVPA and univariate analyses) and thus addresses social-related processing. The sample includes a clearly reported healthy neurotypical adult control group (n=21) analyzed separately from the ASD group. The manuscript reports group-level univariate whole-brain task contrasts and provides mean group effects and coordinate tables/figures (see Additional file 1, Figure S2 and Table S2) for the healthy/control group. Results are presented as voxelwise contrasts and are generalizable to healthy adults. The full text (introduction, methods, results, discussion, and supplementary results) is present. No exclusion criteria are met (not ROI-only, not resting-state/connectivity-only, includes within-group healthy task maps, participants are adults, and this is an empirical fMRI study). Therefore it meets all inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5, and I6 and should be INCLUDED.

This is an fMRI study in healthy adult participants (N=24, ages 22–39) investigating how collective/social schemas influence memory; the paradigm and analyses probe social-related constructs (collective memory, social knowledge, mentalizing-related dmPFC responses). The sample meets the healthy adult criterion. The paper reports group-level, voxelwise whole-brain searchlight results (TFCE-corrected maps; Extended Data Fig.1) derived from regressions of representational similarity metrics, which constitute group-level voxelwise statistical maps generalizable to the healthy group. Results are reported in the main text and extended figures/tables. The study is empirical and includes full methods, results, and discussion, and does not rely solely on ROI, connectivity-only, between-group-only contrasts, or non-empirical approaches. Therefore it satisfies inclusion criteria I3, I4, I5 and I6, and none of the exclusion criteria apply.
